The journey of the Chinese Buddhist monk Faxian, who left Chang'an in 399, in his sixties, to find complete copies of the monastic rules in India, and came home by sea in 412.

With a few companions he crossed the desert past Dunhuang and Khotan and the mountains into northern India. He spent years in the lands of the Gupta Empire, visiting the places of the Buddha's life and copying texts at Pataliputra. He then stayed two years in Sri Lanka before sailing home by way of Southeast Asia, where storms drove his ship off course. He landed on the coast of Shandong.

His account, often called A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms, is one of the few eyewitness descriptions of Gupta India, its towns, hospitals and monasteries. The texts he brought back and translated helped Buddhism take root in China. Later pilgrims such as Xuanzang and Yijing followed his route.
sum: The journey of the Chinese Buddhist monk Faxian, who left Chang'an in 399, in his sixties, to find complete copies of the monastic rules in India, and came home by sea in 412.
